targets.title: Storybook rules
targets.description: Rules for writing Storybook stories and interaction tests for React components in CSF Next: how to query, awaiting interactions, when to use .test() or play, portals, mocks, naming and file setup. Use when writing, fixing or reviewing a .stories.tsx file. Background knowledge that agents preload; not a command.
targets.intro: Apply these rules to every story file you write or review. The first section is always in force; open a rule from the table when the task touches it.

targets.title: Component test rules (React Testing Library)
targets.description: Rules for testing React components with React Testing Library, Vitest and MSW, and for deciding what to test at which layer: rendering, queries, user-event, jest-dom, waitFor, act warnings, mocking the network, flat test files, custom hooks, coverage. Use when writing, fixing or reviewing a *.test.tsx component test or planning a test strategy. Background knowledge that agents preload; not a command.
targets.intro: Apply these rules to every component test you write or review, and to every test strategy you plan. Examples from shared notes may query through Storybook's `canvas`; in React Testing Library use `screen`. For story files, use the Storybook rules instead.

targets.title: Test data builder rules (TypeScript, mimicry-js)
targets.description: Rules for building test data in TypeScript with mimicry-js builders: explicit values for everything a test asserts on, .one() and .many() with overrides and traits, generator placement, fixed() for functions, resetting state. Use when creating or using a builder in a test or story. Background knowledge that agents preload; not a command.
targets.intro: Apply these rules whenever you create or use a builder in a TypeScript test or story.

targets.title: Test data factory rules (Python, factory_boy)
targets.description: Rules for building test data in Python with factory_boy: explicit values for everything a test asserts on, keyword overrides and Traits, build() versus create(), resetting sequences. Use when creating or using a factory in a Python test. Background knowledge that agents preload; not a command.
targets.intro: Apply these rules whenever you create or use a factory in a Python test.

targets.title: Python rules
targets.description: Team conventions for Python code (latest stable release only): docstrings and library documentation, modern typing syntax and mypy strict, exceptions, logging configured at the entry point, asyncio TaskGroup and cancellation, race-safe database writes, t-string and secret-handling security. Use when writing, fixing or reviewing Python code. Background knowledge that agents preload; not a command.
targets.intro: Apply these rules to every Python file you write or review. The first section is always in force; open a rule from the table when the task touches it. Tooling, CI and the project layout are in `python-project-rules`.

targets.title: Python project rules
targets.description: Team conventions for setting up and maintaining a Python project: the latest stable Python, src layout, uv commands, dev dependency groups and a committed lockfile, Ruff for format and lint, a GitHub Actions workflow with uv, a Makefile check target, dependency audit and trusted publishing. Use when creating a Python project, or editing pyproject.toml, CI or tooling. Background knowledge that agents preload; not a command.
targets.intro: Apply these rules when you create a Python project or change its tooling: pyproject.toml, uv, Ruff, CI, the Makefile and publishing. The first section is always in force; open a rule from the table when the task touches it.

targets.title: FastAPI rules
targets.description: Team conventions for structuring, documenting, versioning and testing a FastAPI web API: domain packages, thin routes, services and domain rules, ports, OpenAPI generated from code, response models and error responses, Problem Details errors with 409 versus 422 and a type per error, the 405 Allow header, operation ids, docs exposure, Spectral and oasdiff in CI, Schemathesis, dependency overrides. Use when writing, fixing or reviewing a FastAPI route, service, model or API test, or when starting a new FastAPI service (also load python-rules, python-project-rules and pytest-rules for it). Background knowledge that agents preload; not a command.
targets.intro: Apply these rules to every FastAPI endpoint, service, Pydantic model and API test you write or review. The first section is always in force; open a rule from the table when the task touches it. A new service also needs `python-rules` (logging at the entry point, typing), `python-project-rules` (tooling, CI) and `pytest-rules` (tests): load all three before you write code.

targets.title: pytest rules
targets.description: Team conventions for Python tests with pytest: strict markers, plain assert, expected exceptions, fixture scope, mocking at boundaries, time-machine, testcontainers, pytest-asyncio, Hypothesis, coverage, random order and timeouts. Use when writing, fixing or reviewing a pytest test or test configuration. Background knowledge that agents preload; not a command.
targets.intro: Apply these rules to every Python test you write or review. The first section is always in force; open a rule from the table when the task touches it.
